steps.title: Chemical propellant
steps.prompt: Use dry mass 12,000 kg and Δv = 4,200 m/s in m_prop = m_dry × (exp(Δv/(Isp × g0)) − 1), with Isp = 450 s and g0 = 9.81 m/s². Round to nearest 10 kg.

answerCheck.semantics: Correct if the parsed value rounded to answerFormat equals the reference rounded to answerFormat, or differs from the full reference by at most absoluteTolerance. steps.solution: 4200/(450×9.81) ≈ 0.951410. 12,000×[exp(4200/4414.5)−1] ≈ 19,072.300884 kg, or 19,070 kg to nearest 10. This deliberately incomplete model excludes the later supplies from dry mass.

steps.solution: Chemical: 42×3×5.3 = 667.8 kg. Ion: 140×3×5.3 = 2,226 kg. Difference = 1,558.2 kg. These are Scenario A durations.

notebookBehavior.supportSwitch: Preserve every answer and part when support changes. Both support modes keep access to all hints, templates and solutions.
notebookBehavior.templateUse: Prefilled facts are reference givens. Blank editable cells and starters require learner reasoning; do not auto-copy the candidate exemplar.
notebookBehavior.rounding: Keep full precision for later calculations where possible. If you reuse rounded intermediate values, label this; a consistent rounded partial ledger is also reviewable.

workedExample.title: One panel example, then your turn
steps: Analogous practice case: flux 800 W/m² and efficiency 0.25 give 200 W/m² electrical output.
A 10,000 W load needs 10,000/200 = 50 m² before omitted margins.
Now use Scenario A’s distance-scaled flux and 30,000 W propulsion input.

supportPresentation.guided: Show the worked example, notebook templates and sentence starters initially; hints reveal one at a time and solutions open on request.
supportPresentation.independent: Show full brief and evidence first; the same templates, worked example, starters, hints and solutions remain available on request. No marks or access depend on support/hint use.

limitations: Average speeds are authored rate examples, not outputs of propulsion simulation or actual trajectories.
Food mass, crew and limits are fictional, not recommendations for people.
A lower food mass does not prove a smaller complete spacecraft or a safer mission.
Separate teaching case from the guided constant-rate scenario: the 140-day ion duration is an independent input, not the result of 12 km/s.
Rocket-equation dry mass excludes the later consumables ledger; represented propellant plus supplies is a partial comparison, not a total launch-mass calculation.
Panel hardware mass, life-support energy, thrust history, acceleration, trajectory, redundancy, radiation shielding and safety margins are not modeled.
Constant stellar output, a single distance and idealized constant panel efficiency are assumed; no complete electrical-system adequacy claim.
implementationNotes: Keep legacy mission ID, guided/advanced route IDs and historical 0.1.0-draft. New 0.2.0-draft introduces explicit scenario separation and evidence tasks.
The advanced route is a different task/demand, not merely independent support for the guided route.
Replace displayAnswer threshold rounding with declared per-step answerFormat. Practice checks must distinguish rounded display from full reference precision.
Neither route grants Boreas access; coach outcome is reviewed-only.
The artifact is human-reviewed; no automatic competence, crew-safety or real flight approval.

NASA Dawn provides a real example of efficient low-thrust ion propulsion, and the JPL solar lesson connects array area with distance. Neither validates this fictional crewed case. I need actual trajectory/thrust, full power and mass budgets, redundancy and safety evidence, plus cost and stakeholder/environmental considerations before evaluating a real system.
